calls.prompt:
Edit the first picture, a rough 3D render, into ONE finished building sprite for a pastoral isometric railway game: the Town hall, a two-storey red-brick civic hall with a clock gable and a bell cupola, the SAME building as in the third picture, in the view named under View. Paint over the first picture: its shape, outline, camera and layout stay exactly as they are (every roof, wall, chimney, opening and part where the render has it, nothing added outside its outline or taken out of it), but EVERY surface is painted again in the game's painted style, that of the second picture, the style board: crisp pixel-art-inspired clustered shading, broad readable masses, three or four shades per material, restrained detail, a strong silhouette. The render's surfaces are soft, smeared and patchy, and the walls that the front view never showed were invented by the 3D reconstruction (they are named under View). Paint all of them anew: where the third picture shows a surface, take its stones, bricks, planks, doors, windows and fittings from it, crisp; where the render has invented a surface, paint it as this same building would have it, plausibly and in the same style, from the materials and details of the sides that are known, and never leave it soft, blurred, smeared or plain. The palette family of the whole game: forest green #294638, moss #78804C, oat cream #E4D5B5, limestone #BCA98B, slate #626B6C, teal #477B82, copper #A36B42. Light from the upper left: roofs and tops lightest, lower-left walls mid, lower-right walls darkest (the render's light was corrected for the turn; the painting follows the game's light). Nothing at or above cursor white #ECE4D0 and nothing as strong as selection amber #E8AA48.

Camera: keep the render's camera exactly: orthographic 2:1 isometric, 30 degrees down, ground edges two pixels across for each pixel down, vertical edges vertical, no perspective. Do not rotate, tilt, turn, resize, shift or reshape the building: its silhouette stays where the render's is, and the picture is checked against it. Show the whole building with a clear margin all round, as the render does.

Ground: paint only the building. No plinth, ground, floor slab, grass, shadow or pad under it that the render does not have; keep the foot of the two visible walls plain and straight where the render has it, with no bushes, crates, steps or loose objects added in front of it.

View. The building is turned a quarter turn clockwise seen from above. The front faces the upper left, away from the camera, and nothing of it is in this picture: no entrance door and none of the front's windows or other features on either visible wall. The lower-left wall is the right-hand side; the lower-right wall is the BACK, plainer than the front. The lower-left wall is the right-hand side and is r0's lower-right wall, copied as it stands there: the brick gable end with cream quoins and a stepped parapet, two columns of arched windows on two storeys and the small arched attic window. The lower-right wall is the BACK: a long brick wall as high as the front, with the same cream quoins and string courses and two storeys of arched windows in the front's rhythm, a plain green door instead of the portico, and no clock gable, no planters and no lanterns. The roof is r0's: dark slate, its ridge along the long walls, the two chimney stacks at its two ends, and the bell cupola with its slate dome and gold finial in the middle of the ridge (it shows, centred, in every view); the clock gable is on the front only.

Invented in the first picture (the front view never showed it): the long rear wall (the lower-right wall). Paint these surfaces anew, crisp and plausible, in this building's own materials and details; the first picture's soft or smeared look is not kept.

References: the first is the scaffold's lit render, the picture to paint over; the second is the style board. The third is this building as it is in the game today, seen from the front (view r0): take its materials, details and character from it and paint them over the first picture, surface by surface; the shape, the angle, the outline and the layout are the first picture's and do not change, and the third picture's angle, footprint and any dark glow round it are not used. Paint the SAME building at the size the first picture has it: it is not a mirror image and not a copy of the third picture, and do not paint the third picture again. There, in view r0, the lower-left wall is the front: the long front with the portico, the green double door, the clock gable, the planters and the windows. In this picture the front faces away, hidden behind the building: neither visible wall is the front, and what the front has does not show on them.

Do not paint the plinth itself: no ground, floor slab, pavement, grass or shadow under or around the building. A real RGBA PNG with a transparent background (alpha zero) and opaque building surfaces. Never: rails, trains, people, vehicles, smoke, lettering, signs with text, borders, glow, or loose objects standing apart from the building.

Output size: 1024 x 1024.
